recognize_zh: 年輕病人的骨髓中可見多核且核彼此分離的異常巨核細胞（「pawn-ball」megakaryocytes，CD61 陽性）及微小巨核細胞，合併家族譜系中多人帶 GATA2 p.A286V 並發生 MDS/CMML/AML，再加上疣與非結核分枝桿菌感染病史，應想到 GATA2 缺乏症相關的骨髓腫瘤。
features: Dysplastic megakaryocytes with multiple widely separated round nuclei ('pawn-ball' / osteoclast-like forms) and scattered small hypolobated micromegakaryocytes, highlighted by CD61
Proband marrow: hypercellular core with granulocytic expansion and increased CD34-positive blasts (about 10-12%)
Sister (MDS phase): normocellular marrow with streaming suggesting mild fibrosis, only 1-2% CD34-positive blasts
Dysgranulopoiesis: hypolobated (pseudo-Pelger) and hypogranular neutrophils in blood and aspirate; occasional binucleate megaloblastoid erythroid precursors
Sister (AML transformation): sheets of blasts with folded, cup-like invaginated nuclei, mitoses, and aberrant cytoplasmic NPM1 staining
Ancillary: GATA2 c.857C>T (p.Ala286Val) on Sanger and NGS; trisomy 8 (proband) and der(16)t(1;16) (sister) karyotypes; flow shows CD45-dim CD33+ MPO+ blasts with partial CD34
describe_en: This multi-part case documents a family with germline GATA2 p.A286V. The proband's bone marrow core biopsy is hypercellular with granulocytic expansion and dysplastic megakaryocytes, including small hypolobated forms and multinucleated forms with separated nuclei; CD61 highlights the atypical megakaryocytes and CD34 shows increased blasts (about 10-12%), fitting CMML-2 in the clinical context. The sister's marrow is normocellular with streaming (mild reticulin fibrosis), 1-2% CD34-positive blasts, pseudo-Pelger hypogranular neutrophils, and numerous megakaryocytes with 8 or more widely separated round nuclei ('pawn-ball' megakaryocytes); peripheral blood shows dysplastic neutrophils and a circulating megakaryocyte nuclear fragment. Two years later, her blood and marrow are replaced by blasts with cup-like nuclear invaginations, mitoses, and aberrant cytoplasmic NPM1 expression; flow cytometry shows a CD45-dim blast population (85%) expressing CD33, CD13, MPO, CD123, and partial CD34. Sequencing confirms heterozygous GATA2 c.857C>T in both sisters, and karyotypes show trisomy 8 (proband, post-therapy) and der(16)t(1;16) (sister). Findings are consistent with myeloid neoplasms (CMML, MDS progressing to NPM1/FLT3-mutated AML) arising with germline GATA2 mutation.

ddx.vs: Morphology overlaps completely; germline GATA2 is suggested by young age, prior monocytopenia, warts/mycobacterial infection, and family history, and is confirmed by sequencing a non-hematopoietic (skin fibroblast) sample.

ddx.dx: Myeloid neoplasm with germline RUNX1 or DDX41 mutation
ddx.vs: These also cluster in families, but RUNX1 families have lifelong thrombocytopenia with platelet dysfunction and DDX41 presents at older age with hypocellular MDS, whereas GATA2 shows monocytopenia, B/NK lymphopenia, and immunodeficiency; separation requires germline gene testing.

Megaloblastic change produces hypersegmented rather than hypolobated neutrophils and lacks multinucleated megakaryocytes with widely separated nuclei, CD34 blast increase, or clonal cytogenetic abnormalities.

ddx.dx: AML with NPM1 mutation, de novo
ddx.vs: The cup-like blasts and cytoplasmic NPM1 are identical; the preceding MDS, dysplastic megakaryocytes, and germline GATA2 variant place this case in the germline predisposition category.
